title: Cork and France
summary: Cork's official 2026 county-country pairing with France, presented as the starting point for a student-led local-to-local research project.

statusLabels.label: Local research focus not yet assigned
statusLabels.appliesTo: The specific French region, city, department or county-equivalent to be researched with Cork

statusLabels.label: Research lead
statusLabels.appliesTo: Prompts and possible connections that are not yet established facts

officialUmbrellaPairing.claim: Cork is officially paired with France through Ireland's 2026 EU County Pairings initiative.

localResearchFocus.placeholder: A specific French region, city, department or county-equivalent will be named only after student and editorial agreement.
selectionRequirements: Name one specific locality rather than France as a whole.
Explain why the locality supports a meaningful two-way student investigation.
Record who proposed and approved the focus.
Support the choice with at least one reliable source.
Avoid presenting the local focus as an official government pairing unless an official source explicitly confirms it.

placeholders.corkParticipants: Cork student contributors to be invited
placeholders.franceParticipants: Student contributors connected to the selected French locality to be invited
placeholders.reviewers: Reviewers to be recorded before substantive research is published

studentTeam.displayRule: Do not publish a participant's name, quotation, image or work without recorded permission.

similarities.title: Language learning and exchange
similarities.prompt: Investigate the educational, cultural or civic exchanges that connect Cork with the selected French locality.

similarities.title: Coasts, ports and outward-looking communities
similarities.prompt: If the selected French locality makes this comparison appropriate, examine how coastlines, ports, food and outward-looking communities shape both places.

similarities.title: Student life and local identity
similarities.prompt: Compare how students experience local identity, belonging and European connection in Cork and the selected French locality.

differences.title: Local government and geography
differences.prompt: Compare the scale, geography and civic role of Cork with the selected French locality without assuming the two administrative systems are equivalent.

differences.title: Language in daily life
differences.prompt: Explore how Irish, English, French and any locally relevant languages are encountered in education, public life and identity.

differences.title: Student perspectives
differences.prompt: Invite students in both places to identify a difference that matters to them and support the comparison with context rather than stereotype.

stories.title: Cork's Huguenot history
stories.summary: Investigate whether documented Huguenot histories in Cork can support a carefully sourced local-to-local story after a specific French locality has been selected.
stories.claimBoundary: This is a possible historical research lead. It is not presented as the official reason for the Cork-France pairing, as a verified connection to any particular French locality, or as a finished story.
publicationRequirements: Add reliable sources for every substantive historical claim.
Ask a qualified reviewer to check the interpretation.
Explain the relevance to the selected French locality.
Keep documented fact separate from student reflection.

openQuestions.question: Which specific French locality should students pair with Cork for this research project?
Which student group or educational partner in that locality can research alongside UCC students?
Which three to five similarities and differences can be supported with reliable evidence and student experience?
What reliable archival or scholarly evidence supports a Huguenot story, and does it connect meaningfully to the selected French locality?
What consented student or community story can make the relationship human without replacing evidence?
